market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: Global metallography sample-preparation equipment: $1.2B (2024) to $2.0B by 2033 (7.2%/yr). Broader global metallography equipment market: $650.75M (2025) to $1,120.30M by 2033 (7.03%/yr). Sample-preparation equipment holds ~42.7% share of the overall metallography equipment market. India material testing equipment market (broader, adjacent category): $278.80M (2024) to $415.35M by 2033 (4.18%/yr) per IMARC; a related IMARC estimate cites $290.2M (2025) to $419.6M by 2034 (3.97%/yr); TechSci separately estimates $200.77M (2025) to $271.78M by 2031 (5.02%/yr) — figures vary meaningfully by vendor scope/methodology.
market.domesticSlice: Struers, Buehler, and LECO collectively account for ~40% of the global metallographic sample-cutting-machine market; Indian peer Metkorp offers a full range of metallography equipment domestically but has no disclosed financials.

structureFacts: Rising QC/R&D lab investment in metals, automotive, and aerospace sectors is a cited growth driver for material testing markets
Increasing adoption of automated/digital testing solutions is a stated market trend

Struers, Buehler, and LECO are large multinational players (LECO alone reports ~$310.8M revenue) — far larger in scale than Indian manufacturers, representing an aspirational competitive tier rather than direct scale peers

adoptionStructure.note: Reliability and cost-effectiveness drive sample-preparation equipment's dominant equipment-market share; quality-assurance and regulatory-compliance requirements in metals/materials industries drive purchasing. International trade-show presence (IMTEX, EMO Hannover) is a recurring export-lead-generation channel for Indian manufacturers in this space.
